title: Review a proposed module-boundary change for architectural soundness
description: Given a proposed diff that has a new 'billing' module directly import internal, non-exported functions from the 'users' module's implementation files (rather than its public API), review the change for architectural soundness and identify the boundary violation, its risks, and a concrete corrected design.
acceptanceCriteria: The review explicitly identifies the cross-module import of non-public internals as a boundary violation.
The review explains at least one concrete risk this creates (e.g. breaking billing silently on an unrelated users-module refactor).
The review proposes a concrete corrected design (e.g. an exported public function/interface on the users module that billing should depend on instead).
The review does not flag unrelated, architecturally sound parts of the diff as problems.
verificationMethod: human-review (with architecture-check as a secondary automated signal, e.g. a dependency-boundary linter rule): review is checked against the known injected boundary violation in the fixture diff.
groundTruth: The fixture diff has billing/invoice.js importing directly from users/internal/hash.js instead of a public users/index.js export; the correct design adds a narrow exported function on the users module's public surface and has billing depend only on that.
